title: Podium Larry Alternatives for Service Businesses
seo_title: Podium Larry Alternatives: Compare Options & Fit
description: Compare Podium Larry alternatives for service businesses: Off The Clock AI, Sameday, Avoca and Jobber. Pricing, platform fit and job quoting.
intro: You want the call answered and the job priced. That does not have to become a decision about replacing your entire business system.
verdict: Choose Off The Clock when you want an AI operator that answers, quotes and books—not another platform for running technicians and invoices. QuoteDone brings your prices to the phone and your website.
reason: Podium’s home-services package combines Larry with field-service management, dispatch, customer history and payments. That is a broader purchase than replacing the person who answers the phone. [[podium-plans]]

Larry already has price-book access and can communicate service fees. The distinction is not “can it say a price?” It is whether the customer receives the price of the job they described, including the details that change it. [[podium-larry]]

Off The Clock centers that conversation. Business questions, booking, transfers and follow-up come with the operator; QuoteDone adds calculation from the owner’s rates and the customer’s actual job details. You choose the pricing. The customer does not have to wait for you to repeat the intake.
choices: Job quotes without a replacement FSM

Your existing tools can remain the home for field operations. QuoteDone handles supported project prices during the inquiry and through its website widget. This is a separate operator subscription, not a native Podium integration.

Sameday’s directory lists ServiceTitan, Jobber, FieldRoutes and Service Fusion. That makes its integration coverage a concrete difference from the bundled Podium offer; the actions supported by each connection still matter. [[sameday-integrations]]
Inbound calls plus coaching and human backup

Avoca combines inbound handling with call coaching and a documented trained-CSR backup program. Those capabilities address how a team handles and reviews conversations; they are not interchangeable with calculating the customer’s project price. [[avoca-coach]] [[avoca-human]]

Receptionist is part of the Jobber account, with an eligible-plan add-on and unlimited usage on Plus. This is a comparison for a business using or selecting Jobber—not a standalone alternative to all of Podium’s modules. [[jobber-help]]
decision: Choose Off The Clock to change what gets finished during the customer inquiry—not to move every part of your business into another system. Your rates, the complete requested job, and the next appointment belong in the same conversation.
faqs: Can Podium Larry give customers prices?
Yes. Podium describes price-book access and service-fee communication. A measured, multi-item project calculation is a separate capability from stating a configured service fee. [[podium-larry]]
Does Off The Clock replace my field-service software?

No. It is the operator and QuoteDone offer, not a replacement dispatch, invoicing or technician-management platform. Any connection to your existing software must match the integration actually available for your setup.
card_description: Larry’s advertised package includes an FSM. Compare that purchase with a separate operator, connected scheduling and QuoteDone’s job pricing.
sections: A visible price for the operator and QuoteDone
QuoteDone is $279 per month with 1,200 included minutes, the AI operator and website quote widget. Additional usage is $0.35 per minute. There is no setup fee in the Off The Clock offer.

Podium’s reviewed home-services plan does not publish a numerical subscription price. Its sales-quoted bundle includes an FSM, so there is no credible dollar-for-dollar saving to calculate from that page. Off The Clock’s advantage here is a defined offer without making a new field-service platform part of the purchase. [[podium-plans]]
The difference shows up in the scope
A customer asking about mowing with edging is not asking only for the base mowing price. The selected edging, its measured length and the business’s own charge all belong in that request.

QuoteDone’s rule is to price the supported complete scope or preserve it for owner review. An unknown length does not become an average, and an unpriced extra does not disappear. That keeps your pricing authority intact while moving routine inquiries away from your phone.
